title: Two power-contract limits were copied incorrectly in a Board report

beats.text: A company was hired to schedule electricity purchases.

visual.sub: Original authority separated electricity from administrative fees

beats.text: The contract separated market charges from administrative fees.

visual.kicker: Original authority separated electricity from administrative fees

beats.text: The original agreement allowed $4,242,800 for scheduling services.

visual.label: Original authority separated electricity from administrative fees

beats.text: A signed amendment raised the market charge limit to $255,500,000.

visual.label: The first amendment raised the market payment cap

beats.text: The administrative allowance stayed the same.

visual.kicker: The first amendment raised the market payment cap

beats.text: Two years later, the historical comparison copied two figures incorrectly.

visual.kicker: Two prior limits were transcribed incorrectly in 2025

beats.text: One figure was $500,000 below the original agreement.

visual.label: Two prior limits were transcribed incorrectly in 2025

beats.text: The first amendment was understated by $30,000,000.

visual.label: Two prior limits were transcribed incorrectly in 2025

beats.text: The totals in the exhibit still matched the signed agreements.
Later authority covered multiple years of volatile market charges.

visual.kicker: Later approval extended the term and raised the ceiling

beats.text: The analyst reported $319,242,674 spent in the first three years.

visual.label: Later approval extended the term and raised the ceiling

beats.text: The Controller’s two payment tables agree to the cent.
There are 476 vouchers for this contract.
The vouchers classify the spending as power for resale.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
